exposure: Admission to neonatal intensive care unit (yes/no)
cohort: Mothers of children with ASD visiting Beni-Suef University Hospital in Egypt (n=268) and mothers of children without ASD attending a primary school with a kindergarten in Egypt (n=504)
finding: In a case-control study in Egypt, various maternal factors (urban residence, relative father, diabetes, previous abortion, assisted fertility, family history of ASD, multiple pregnancy, passive smoking, vaginal bleeding, hypertension, preterm labor) and neonatal factors (convulsions, NICU admission) were associated with increased odds of ASD, while vitamin intake during pregnancy and C-section were associated with decreased odds.
mod_finding: C-section was associated with decreased odds of ASD.
followup_time: Likely preschool or early school age
